children: Shares of Voltas Ltd fell as much as 3.7 percent in intraday trade on Monday. Brokerages flagged concerns over weak margins and earnings quality following the company's Q2 FY27 results, despite strong growth in its air conditioning business.

Voltas stock recovered some losses to trade 1.2 percent lower at Rs 1,044 in late morning deals. Goldman Sachs maintained a Sell rating with a target price of Rs 1,025, implying a downside of around 3 percent from Friday's close. Nomura retained a Neutral rating with a target of Rs 1,199, indicating a potential upside of 13 percent, but warned that intensifying competition could delay margin recovery.
Goldman Sachs flags weak earnings quality

Goldman Sachs said Voltas' Q2 revenue was broadly in line with its estimates, but earnings missed expectations and EBITDA quality remained weak. The brokerage added that the Unitary Cooling Products (UCP) business delivered strong volume-led growth, supported by market share gains in room air conditioners and Voltbek home appliances. However, the recovery in UCP margins was weaker than expected.

Margins in the Electro-Mechanical Projects and Services (EMPS) segment benefited from a one-off write-back, while the Engineering Products and Services business continued to perform strongly.
Voltas implemented an additional price increase in room air conditioners in October, with management expecting UCP margins to improve from the fourth quarter.
Nomura cuts earnings estimates, warns of margin pressure

Nomura maintained its Neutral rating, citing risks to profitability despite a favourable demand outlook. The brokerage expects industry-wide AC volumes to grow 25 percent in FY27 and 15 percent in FY28, supported by warmer weather conditions and a favourable base. This could drive UCP revenue growth of 31 percent and 22 percent, respectively, for Voltas.
However, Nomura cautioned that the company's focus on market share over profitability, alongside rising competition, could constrain margin recovery.

It consequently reduced its UCP margin estimates to 5.7 percent for FY27, 7.5 percent for FY28 and 8 percent for FY29, representing cuts of 130, 100 and 100 basis points, respectively. These revisions prompted Nomura to lower its earnings per share estimates by 12 percent for FY27 and 7 percent each for FY28 and FY29.
Voltas Q2 profit rises 53%, AC volumes jump 32%

Voltas reported a 53.4 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 52.6 crore for Q2 FY27, while revenue rose 15.3 percent to Rs 2,707 crore, exceeding the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of Rs 2,556 crore. EBITDA surged 82.2 percent to Rs 128.3 crore, beating the poll estimate of Rs 92 crore. The EBITDA margin expanded to 4.7 percent from 3 percent a year earlier, ahead of the estimated 3.6 percent.

The company's room air conditioner business recorded 32 percent volume growth during the quarter. Voltas retained its market leadership with a 17.4 percent year-to-date share as of September 2026, maintaining a 4.2 percentage-point lead over its nearest competitor.
Voltas shares have declined 24.4 percent so far in 2026, significantly underperforming the Nifty 50's 4.8 percent fall. The company's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 34,600 crore.
